description: Bright, legible architectural exterior development with controlled highlights, natural sky, and realistic material depth.

exposure.instruction: Increase overall exposure decisively to create a bright, welcoming exterior while retaining detail in sunlit walls, glazing, and pale paving.

shadows.instruction: Open deep shadows beneath roof overhangs, along building bases, and in the foreground; retain believable architectural depth.

highlights.instruction: Recover highlight detail in render, walls, glazing, and other bright existing surfaces; prevent clipping without dulling sunlight.

contrast.instruction: Restore crisp architectural tonal separation after shadow recovery without HDR compression or exaggerated local contrast.

whiteBalance.instruction: Neutralize unwanted casts and warm only enough to make stone, plaster, and wood inviting while keeping neutral building materials believable.

vibrance.instruction: Enrich muted existing color clearly while preserving natural variation between vegetation, sky, stone, plaster, and wood.

saturation.instruction: Increase saturation only with controlled channel separation; preserve realistic greens, blue sky, and neutral façades.

texture.instruction: Reveal existing stone, plaster, and wood texture through tonal richness; do not redraw or invent surface detail.

clarity.instruction: Add moderate, clean architectural clarity for legibility without halos, crunchy surfaces, or edge glow.

sharpness.instruction: Apply only light final sharpening with natural edges.

materialPriorities.instruction: Enrich dull existing grass toward a rich natural green while preserving blade, dry-area, hue, and luminance variation; never fluorescent or uniform.
Deepen only the existing sky while preserving real clouds, highlight roll-off, atmosphere, and time of day.
Reveal existing stone texture, earth tones and tonal richness without crunchy microcontrast.
Keep existing wood warm, rich and realistic without an orange or red cast.
